content:
morgan: Heads up — canary bringing up mirrored replicas for quantized v1.2.0 is showing structured JSON truncation for funcalls in ~0.6% of requests.
nana: Do you mean token split (unicode) mid-JSON or a shard/replica boundary cut?
morgan: Replica-boundary. Example: final payload becomes truncated like: '{\"tool\": {\"name\": \"search\", \"args\": ' and then nothing. Downstream parser fails and we sometimes invoke rescue that retries the tool — risky.
tariq: Can you paste repro + captured stream chunks?
morgan: Repro is simple: mirrored streaming enabled, send funcall-heavy prompt. Captured stream (chunks in order of arrival):
```
chunk#1 from replica B: '{"type":"chunk","seq":1,"data":"{\"id\":\"r1\",\"content\":\"...\"}"}'
chunk#2 from replica A: '{"type":"chunk","seq":5,"data":"{\"tool\": {\"name\": \"search\", \"args\": {\"q\": \"cats\"}, \"call\": true}}'  // final fragment'
chunk#3 from replica B: '{"type":"chunk","seq":3,"data":"...rest..."}'
```
evan: This aligns with a reordering issue: stitcher currently concatenates by arrival time, not strict seq reorder. Network jitter caused seq 5 to arrive early.
morgan: We do carry seq ids but the reordering buffer was small to cut tail latency — so sometimes we accept out-of-order to keep latency SLOs. That optimization is exactly the tradeoff biting us.
nana: Options: 1) enforce a reorder buffer N ms, 2) mark 'final_chunk' in stream envelope so stitcher knows a chunk completes JSON, 3) introduce a conservative parsing healer that can merge adjacent partial JSON tokens and attempt recovery.
tariq: Reorder buffer helps but increases p50/p95 slightly. Final_chunk flag seems clean and cheap if model runtime can emit it. Does our runtime support emitting a terminator?
morgan: We can add it at runtime by wrapping the replica's stream with an envelope, yes. Prototyped 'json-healer' approach (regex & incremental parse) recovered ~80% of these cases in canary — but it sometimes invents structure if the token boundary is in the middle of a string, so safety concerns exist.
evan: Important: never auto-heal when funcall implies side effects (webhooks/db writes). For those cases we must fail closed and surface to caller or retry idempotently. Healer only for read-only evals and tests.
morgan: Agreed. I added a quick tag 'toolcall_metadata.safe_to_auto_repair' boolean to the call contract, default false. Healer only runs when true.
nana: Also we need a regression harness in onboarding: simulate mirrored replicas with programmable network delay and out-of-order chunk delivery; assert final JSON parse success or a controlled safe fallback. I'll add it to the onboarding CI.
morgan: Filed ML ticket: <https://redwood.internal/issue/ML-3284|ML-3284> with stack traces and canary logs. Patch includes reorder buffer bump + optional final_chunk flag + json-healer behind a runtime flag.
deploy-bot: deploy started for patch/reorder-buffer@canary — build 2026.3.14.5
tariq: :thumbsup: Also add metrics: structured_parse_heal_attempts, structured_parse_heal_success, and toolcall_auto_repair_blocked_by_side_effect. We need to correlate with model version and quantization setting.
morgan: Will add telemetry and an evalset that runs quantized models on canary for 8h overnight to gather parse-fail rate before/after.
evan: One more: add a deterministic stitch test that ensures chunk ordering is correct even when seq ids are delayed by clock drift. Covers clock skew.
morgan: Yep — putting that in the RFC. TL;DR: root cause = streaming assembly race when mirrored replicas stream chunks; short-term = healer behind flag for safe calls; mid-term = final_chunk flag + stricter seq reordering. Will report back with overnight numbers tomorrow.
